group_scores.rationale: In-window T1 prints confirm energy pass-through: euro-area HICP 4.0%, core revised up to 2.6%, energy +21%; UK CPI 3.6% with motor fuels +33.2%; euro-area IP -1.5% y/y. Offsets: the flash was unchanged, UK CPI came in below consensus, bank RoE is at a decade high, and no ECB December signal was given in the window (Vujcic and Lagarde speeches). Verifier note: STOXX 600 fell every session 16-20 Nov (-5.8% local), while MSCI World fell about 8.1%. That contradicts the lead's 'one-day lag' explanation and its assumed relative underperformance, so the direction is ambiguous. Score stays 0.
group_scores.falsifier: Hawkish ECB repricing (December 50bp or a series of hikes) while growth weakens, EUR/USD below about 1.08, or OAT-Bund widening on a French budget crisis would mean -1. Europe outperforming during a renewed US AI sell-off would mean +1.

group_scores.rationale: FX drag from EUR (-0.56%) and GBP (about -0.8%) was partly offset by the yen (+0.85%). No SNB, RBA, Riksbank or Norges Bank decisions fell in the window. Japan core CPI was 2.2%, not a surprise, and BoJ hawkishness came only from Takata, a dissenter. UK borrowing YTD is below last year despite record October debt interest. The policy-tightening regime predates the window.
group_scores.falsifier: A BoJ hike signal from Ueda, broadening USD strength combined with higher energy prices, or the 30y gilt moving well above 5.7% would mean -1.

group_scores.rationale: No Europe or DM event in the window changes VWRA.L against the world. The issuer page shows no notice and NAV published normally through 20 Nov. The weekly drawdown came from the US AI shock (Nvidia CEO resignation, 19 Nov), outside this pillar's remit. Because VT is the yardstick, the score is 0 by construction.
group_scores.falsifier: A gilt or OAT funding crisis, an ECB reserve-requirement shock to bank funding, or a VWRA fee, index or structure change would require a revisit.
